title: DSH trusted-local acceptance definition v2 (Windows, no sandbox)

derived_from.derivation_statement: v2 is DERIVED from v1 and does not replace it. v1 stays frozen with its verdicts and its CMP-04/CMP-13 contradiction intact. The per-case provenance of every carried, rewritten, split or unclaimed invariant is in acceptance-spec.trusted-local-v2.provenance.json.

trust_model.name: trusted-local
trust_model.one_line: The OS user account is the execution authority boundary.
trust_model.statement: DSH runs as the invoking Windows user with no sandbox, no WSL, no Linux VM and no SSH execution world. Every process it starts -- including the IPython kernel -- runs as that same OS user with that user's full filesystem, network and process visibility. This deployment therefore claims NO confinement of reads, writes, network or process visibility, and no case in this spec may be read as establishing one. What this deployment does claim is bounded and checkable: identity, composition, one programmable execution surface, correct data and recovery behaviour, bounded concurrency, honest verification, and research provenance.
explicitly_not_claimed: host-secret read isolation (any process can read any file the OS user can read)
network / egress isolation (there is no OS or gateway boundary)
filesystem write confinement (danger-full-access means no write restriction either)
a second execution world, and therefore any cross-world path consistency or role transition
verification-environment privilege separation from the host
trust_model.sandbox_rows_retained_because: The pinned DSH ABI requires them. `sandboxPolicy` is a SERVICE that seven entries inject, and `inject` is a readiness gate: deleting the row leaves those entries permanently pending, cascades so that shell/fs/ptcRuntime never publish, and the preset fails to mount with the model's tool face at ZERO. MEASURED. The rows are therefore configured as `danger-full-access`, which is DSH's own first-class path (ConfinedSandboxMode EXCLUDES it by type).
trust_model.identity_boundary: compatibility.lock.json -> deployment.identity. Every case below is bound to that identity. A PASS recorded against another identity is not a PASS for this one.

layer_legend.T0: pure function / type level; no DSH service involved
layer_legend.T1: production DSH services with a mock provider
layer_legend.T2: the actual built host / profile / preset, booted
layer_legend.T3: real subprocess kill and real disk recovery
layer_legend.T4: real OS boundary; under trusted-local this observes behaviour, it does not establish confinement
layer_legend.T5: authorized live provider driving real children (BLOCKED_EXTERNAL while live_provider_budget_authorized is false)
layer_legend.T6: a real coding or research task end to end

case_shape.id: family prefix + 2-digit ordinal; v1 ids are REUSED where the case carries over
case_shape.requirement: the invariant this case is about
case_shape.stimulus: the exact thing an operator does to the system
case_shape.oracle: the observation that decides PASS, naming its own failure case
case_shape.mandatory: true for every case in this definition
case_shape.dependencies: case ids this case's own text refers to, derived mechanically
case_shape.definition_version: the definition revision this case was authored at

no_status_rule: THIS FILE CARRIES NO STATUS, NO EVIDENCE PATH AND NO VERDICT. Results live under qualification/results/<qualification-contract-id>/. The separation is what allows a result to be filed without changing this file's digest, and therefore without invalidating the qualification contract identity it is bound to. In v1 the spec was BOTH an identity input and the evidence ledger, so filing evidence broke the identity check -- measured: the live ledger's digest moved across 11 revisions.
mandatory_rule: Every case in this file is mandatory.

verdict_vocabulary.NOT_RUN: no verdict has been filed for this case under this contract identity.
verdict_vocabulary.PASS: the oracle was established, and the verdict names the evidence that establishes it under this contract identity.
verdict_vocabulary.FAIL: the contract CLAIMS this invariant, it was measured, and it was not established. A FAIL asserts a claim, so a FAIL may not be filed against an invariant the contract does not claim.
verdict_vocabulary.NOT_CLAIMED: the contract deliberately does NOT claim this invariant. This is a first-class verdict and NOT a soft FAIL: it asserts that no claim is being made, and the record must name what would have to be true for the claim to exist. It exists so a deleted claim can be stated honestly instead of being forced into PASS or FAIL. NOT_CLAIMED may not be used to retire an inconvenient FAIL without naming the topology fact that makes the invariant inapplicable.
verdict_vocabulary.BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: the case needs an external resource that is not authorized (live_provider_budget_authorized is false). A recorded blocker, never a PASS.
verdict_vocabulary.REUSED_EVIDENCE: not a verdict: a BINDING of an existing v1 evidence artifact to a v2 case under the E3 reuse rule. It accompanies a PASS or a FAIL and never substitutes for one.

families.name: IDENTITY
families.subject: What this deployment IS. Artifact identity, spec identity, and the rule that no old verdict migrates.

families.name: COMPOSITION
families.subject: How the host profile and agent preset are assembled, including the retained sandbox rows at danger-full-access and the real model-visible tool surface.

families.name: IPYTHON
families.subject: The persistent IPython kernel as the PRIMARY programmable execution surface: real shell, persistent namespace, one tool with one parameter, host-owned lifecycle, bounded output, visible epochs.

families.name: NATIVE BRIDGE
families.subject: The path from a Python cell to a native DSH tool: one shared policy pipeline, dynamic revocation, reference delivery, no forged host facts, bounded nesting.

families.name: DATA
families.subject: Capture, paging, integrity and gap attribution for observations and artifacts, including the model-visible projection bound.

families.name: RECOVERY
families.subject: Crash, kill, stale-epoch and hostile-checkpoint behaviour; unknown outcomes stay unknown.

families.name: FILESYSTEM
families.subject: Filesystem behaviour under trusted-local. These cases check CORRECTNESS and HONEST DISCLOSURE, never confinement -- there is no confinement to check.

families.name: CONCURRENCY
families.subject: The hard child capacity, all admission paths, real top-up, unknown occupancy, root non-starvation and credit atomicity.

families.name: VERIFICATION
families.subject: Verification integrity: zero tests, skips, oracle tampering, receipt freshness, A-B-A, in-flight writers, tier honesty.

families.name: RESEARCH
families.subject: Search-to-citation provenance: real sources, evidence tiers, incomplete parses, truncation, raw/derived separation, claim location.

families.name: CACHE/OBSERVABILITY
families.subject: Observation caching, history watermarks and the three separate visibilities (obtainable / consumed / model-projected).

cases.requirement: artifact identity locked
cases.stimulus: Boot the built launcher `node apps/cli/lib/bin.js --profile daily-candidate`, then swap it for a different build or load `src/` instead of `lib/`, and repeat the first successful tool call.
cases.oracle: The first tool call actually succeeds and the resolved module graph is recorded: every `@deepseek-ai/*` specifier resolves under `D:\DSH\src\dsh-src\packages\*\lib\`, and sha256 of the launcher equals `deployment.inputs.artifact_sha256`. A run whose only success is `--help`, or whose graph mixes `src` and `lib`, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: identity recomputes from its inputs
cases.stimulus: Recompute sha256 over `json.dumps(deployment.inputs, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True)` from the file on disk, and separately change one byte of one input and recompute.
cases.oracle: The recomputed digest equals `deployment.identity` character for character, and the one-byte change produces a different digest. A recorded identity that no script on disk can reproduce is NOT PASS, even if it looks well-formed.

cases.requirement: no verdict migrates from the old specs
cases.stimulus: Load `qualification/gates.json` (104 old cases, 85 PASS) and `qualification/specs/acceptance-spec.json` (112 old cases) alongside this file, and compare every id, name and subject.
cases.oracle: Zero old case ids appear in this file with any status other than NOT_RUN, and zero evidence entries are carried across. The comparison is by id, by requirement name and by subject matter; a PASS that arrives without its own evidence file under this identity is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: spec digest is pinned as an identity input
cases.stimulus: Change one character of this spec file, then re-read `deployment.inputs.trusted_local_acceptance_spec_sha256` and the recomputed identity.
cases.oracle: The stored digest no longer matches the file and the recomputed identity no longer matches `deployment.identity`, and a reader can detect both without trusting prose. A spec edited in place while the identity stays put is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: public export boundary compiles under the strict config, with no cast hiding an undefined value
cases.stimulus: Compile all production packages and tests with `tsconfig.check.json` (the config that INCLUDES `src/**/*.test.ts`), then inject one type error into a test file and recompile. Then scan for `as never` in both plugin and config position.
cases.oracle: The clean tree exits 0 and the injected error makes the compile FAIL. A green run under `tsconfig.json` alone is NOT PASS, because that config excludes the test files. TWO IDIOMS ARE NAMED so this clause is decidable without a judgement call: (a) `ctx.plugin(plugin as never, cfg as never)` -- the cast on the PLUGIN argument is noise, because `ctx.plugin(plugin, cfg)` compiles clean; (b) `ctx.plugin(Storage, {} as never)` -- in CONFIG position the cast MASKS a true diagnostic (`Argument of type '{}' is not assignable to parameter of type 'undefined'`), and the argument should be OMITTED. A config-position `as never` is NOT PASS. `as never` must NEVER be replaced by `as any`, which trades a visible cast for an invisible one. No non-null `!` may be used to hide a genuinely undefined value; no private symbol may be deep-imported across a package boundary.

cases.requirement: the pinned checkout is unmodified
cases.stimulus: Run `git status --porcelain` and `git rev-parse HEAD` inside `D:\DSH\src\dsh-src`.
cases.oracle: The working tree is clean and HEAD equals `ddefc45fbc7f8e46dd73185e68295696d1297887`. Any tracked modification, any staged change, or a moved HEAD is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the composed profile activates every entry
cases.stimulus: Boot the composed daily profile from a foreign cwd and read the activation report.
cases.oracle: Zero entries report `did not activate`, `pending`, or `waiting for services`; the boot output contains no `warning: N entries did not activate` line. The measured count is recorded verbatim.

cases.requirement: the sandbox rows exist and are explicitly danger-full-access
cases.stimulus: Read the resolved config graph for the `sandbox-policy` row and the effective sandbox mode of a live session.
cases.oracle: A row with `id: sandbox-policy` is present (NOT deleted), its configured mode is `danger-full-access`, and its `workspaceRoot` resolves to an absolute path. The row being absent is a specific known failure: it leaves seven entries pending and drives the tool face to zero.

cases.requirement: no silent degradation to danger-full-access
cases.stimulus: Remove the sandbox provider row(s) and boot, then separately boot the normal configuration and read `defaultMode`, any session override, and `resolve().mode`.
cases.oracle: With the provider missing, the loader FAILS with an explicit error naming the missing provider and does NOT boot with an unwrapped argv or an implicit danger-full-access. In the normal boot the three values are separately observable, and the deployment default is recorded as EXPLICITLY CONFIGURED rather than a fallback. A boot that cannot distinguish an explicitly configured danger-full-access from a provider-missing fallback is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the model-visible tool surface is intact and named
cases.stimulus: Boot the real profile from a cwd unrelated to the profile directory, using a probe that adds NO row, and read the model-visible catalog for one real session. Record the count and the full name set verbatim.
cases.oracle: The model-visible tool surface is intact and named, and the tool count is MEASURED AND RECORDED IN THE EVIDENCE rather than pinned in this oracle. The catalog for one real Session, measured through a probe that INSERTS NO TOOL ROW, must show `ipython` present, `work` present, `pwsh` absent, `error` null, and `presetRoots` naming the home that was actually booted. A catalog measured through a verification overlay that inserts the tool row does NOT establish this case. The measured count is recorded verbatim in the evidence, together with the full measured name set, so a change in composition is VISIBLE as a diff without being a failure of this case. A pinned integer is deliberately NOT a pass condition here: the v1 oracle pinned `toolCountAgentKey is 28`, and that pin -- not the product -- is what created v1's contradiction with CMP-13.

cases.requirement: the preset root is anchored at the profile, not at cwd
cases.stimulus: Boot the same installed profile from an unrelated cwd, then repeat with a cwd-relative preset root.
cases.oracle: In the anchored case the preset `daily-standard` resolves and the resolved root is absolute and derived from the profile's own directory. In the cwd-relative case the preset is NOT found and the tool count is 0. The failure direction is recorded, not just the success direction.

cases.requirement: approval policy matches the mode and is not model-writable
cases.stimulus: Read the effective approval policy under the deployed mode, then attempt to change it from a session.
cases.oracle: The effective policy is `never` and is declared explicitly in the profile patch rather than inherited from a workspace-write-era default. A model-originated attempt to change it has no effect and is recorded.

cases.requirement: a patch replaces the whole config object
cases.stimulus: Patch exactly one field of a row that carries several fields, then dump the resolved row config.
cases.oracle: The dumped row carries every required key with its intended value, and no unmentioned key has silently reverted to a schema default. A dump showing a lost sibling key is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: two presets sharing one composition file stay separate
cases.stimulus: Mount two presets from the same composition file in parallel sessions and compare their tool catalogs and module-scope state.
cases.oracle: Each agent's catalog contains exactly its own rows, and no module-scope state crosses sessions. Shared module state is reported as the measured constraint it is, not smoothed over.

cases.requirement: two roots on one standing scope do not contaminate each other
cases.stimulus: Two roots on the same preset interleave `work` calls.
cases.oracle: Each run's tasks, credit reservation and cancellation are fully separated; no task id, reservation or tombstone appears in the other run's record.

cases.requirement: bundle and preset own different halves
cases.stimulus: Install the extension as a bundle and boot the composed profile; read the registration log.
cases.oracle: The host-scoped row is registered exactly once (no duplicate registration error, no second handle) and the agent-scoped tool row comes from the preset. A design where both the bundle and the profile insert the same host row is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the ipython tool is carried by the product
cases.stimulus: Perform a fresh install following the documented procedure, then boot with a probe that adds NO row and read the catalog.
cases.oracle: The real session catalog holds `ipython`, and the probe's `presetRoots` confirms the home that was booted. Evidence produced by an overlay that INSERTED the row proves the tool works without proving the product carries it, and is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: home overrides are visible in the resolved graph
cases.stimulus: Place a home patch that would change the model or the preset, and boot both the canary home and the stock control home.
cases.oracle: The resolved graph shows the override explicitly for the canary home, and the stock control uses an uncontaminated home whose graph shows no such override.

cases.requirement: the shell leaves the daily preset
cases.stimulus: Read the daily preset's model-visible tool catalog from a real boot and record the full tool name set verbatim.
cases.oracle: The architecture requires the model-facing shell to leave the daily preset, so `pwsh` (and any equivalent shell tool) must be ABSENT from the daily catalog while `ipython` is present. The full measured name set is recorded. A catalog that still contains `pwsh` is NOT PASS, and the record must state the measured set rather than the intended one.

cases.requirement: launcher args are redacted and identity-bound
cases.stimulus: Read `deployment.inputs.launcher_args_redacted` and compare the named profile with the profile whose digest is an identity input.
cases.oracle: The recorded args are the redacted form, contain no credential material, and name the profile whose patch digest is `deployment.inputs.host_profile_digest`. A raw argument string carrying a key or a token is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a real IPython shell, not a CPython imitation
cases.stimulus: In one cell, evaluate `get_ipython()` and execute a supported magic such as `%who` or `%time`.
cases.oracle: `get_ipython()` returns a real IPython shell object and the magic executes. A plain-CPython interpreter that fails either is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the namespace persists across cells
cases.stimulus: Cell 1 builds a DataFrame, a function and an import; cell 2 uses all three without redefining them.
cases.oracle: All three are available in cell 2. The record shows cell 2's source does not contain the definitions, so the persistence is real rather than the earlier input being re-read.

cases.requirement: top-level await works with no wrapper
cases.stimulus: `await` an asyncio task and a native tool call at top level in one cell.
cases.oracle: Both settle with accurate results and the cell source contains no `async def` / function-body wrapper.

cases.requirement: an exception leaves partial state and does not claim rollback
cases.stimulus: Assign a variable, then raise in the same cell; read the variable in the next cell.
cases.oracle: The error is reported with its traceback AND the assignment is still present in the next cell. Any wording that presents the cell as rolled back is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: stdin is disabled and fails fast
cases.stimulus: Execute `input()` and `getpass()` in cells.
cases.oracle: Each fails promptly with an explainable error and the cell settles; it never waits for input and never holds the execution slot open.

cases.requirement: only the matching reply and idle settle a cell
cases.stimulus: Interleave shell and iopub frames carrying other msg_ids while a cell runs, and restart the kernel mid-sequence.
cases.oracle: The cell is completed only by its own reply plus idle; a foreign frame does not complete it, and the number of ignored foreign frames is reported. Cross-cell association by parent_header and epoch is demonstrated, not asserted.

cases.requirement: interrupt then reuse, with honest outcome classification
cases.stimulus: Interrupt a pure-Python CPU loop; separately interrupt a cell suspended on `await`; then run a further cell in the same kernel.
cases.oracle: The CPU loop settles after the interrupt. A suspended cell that does not settle is reported as `unknown` with a reset and an epoch advance, and the record states that this is NOT a graceful KeyboardInterrupt. The kernel is usable afterwards. A report that presents the suspended case as cleanly cancelled is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a natural activation end rebinds or reports loss explicitly
cases.stimulus: A continuable child ends its activation and the session legitimately continues.
cases.oracle: The kernel is either legitimately rebound to the continuing session, or the epoch loss is stated explicitly with what was lost. A silent restart presented as continuity is NOT PASS. This case needs a live provider and is expected BLOCKED_EXTERNAL while `live_provider_budget_authorized` is false.

cases.requirement: one tool, one parameter, no lifecycle surface
cases.stimulus: Enumerate the model-facing ipython surface in a real boot and search the tree for lifecycle tool names.
cases.oracle: Exactly ONE tool named `ipython` exists, with exactly ONE parameter `code`; no `ipython_open`/`ipython_send`/`ipython_read`/`ipython_status`/`ipython_close` and no `python_exec` alias is registered anywhere. The measured parameter list is recorded.

cases.requirement: the model cannot own kernel lifecycle
cases.stimulus: From inside a cell, attempt to start, restart, shut down or evict the kernel; attempt to raise the output cap or cell timeout; attempt to read the connection file.
cases.oracle: Every attempt is refused or has no effect, and each attempt is recorded individually. Kernel lifecycle, output cap and timeout remain host-side decisions.

cases.requirement: the kernel cwd is the project root
cases.stimulus: Read `os.getcwd()` inside a cell for a session started for a known project root, and resolve a relative path from it.
cases.oracle: The reported cwd is the project root the session was started for, recorded verbatim, and the relative path resolves inside it. A temp-directory cwd is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: output is bounded and the loss is stated
cases.stimulus: Print substantially more than the output cap from one cell, including one very long line.
cases.oracle: The projection says TRUNCATED, names the true total bytes produced, and names a spill path when one exists. The model is never handed a silent prefix. The cap value in force is recorded.

cases.requirement: late output is classified separately and never rides another cell
cases.stimulus: A background thread writes to stdout after the cell has returned; then start another cell while the thread is still writing.
cases.oracle: The post-return write is reported as late/unattributed and does not appear in any later cell's result. A write landing DURING a later cell is reported as undecidable rather than attributed. A claim that the originating cell's parent id is always preserved is NOT PASS, because it is false for a thread started with an empty context.

cases.requirement: kernel death is visible and nothing is replayed
cases.stimulus: Hold variables in the kernel, then kill the kernel process; run a further cell in the same session.
cases.oracle: The next result reports a NEW kernel epoch with a reason, states that the volatile state from the previous epoch is LOST, and states that nothing was replayed. The Session itself survives and remains usable.

cases.requirement: the kernel transport is authenticated and frames are bounded
cases.stimulus: Read the transport facts for a live kernel (transport kind, encryption, connection-file permissions) and send an over-limit frame in each direction; then send a normal cell and record whether the kernel is still usable.
cases.oracle: The transport is IPC or TCP with CurveZMQ keys and encryption required; a plaintext-TCP start is recorded as a FINDING and is NOT PASS. An over-limit frame is REFUSED in both directions -- the encoder refuses to emit it and the decoder refuses on the DECLARED length before buffering -- and the refusal is a structured, machine-readable outcome naming the byte limit in force and the declared length that exceeded it. The kernel remains usable after the refusal. An over-limit frame that is silently dropped, silently truncated, or presented as empty output is NOT PASS. A `droppedFrames`-style drop-and-continue counter is explicitly NOT required: a failed transport is a failed OPERATION, not a partial successful observation.

cases.requirement: one shared policy pipeline for every call route
cases.stimulus: Call the same native tool three ways: directly by the model, through the programmatic/PTC path, and from an IPython cell.
cases.oracle: Approval decision, guard decision, returned schema and final value are identical across all three routes, and no route reaches the executor without passing the guard. A route with a bypass is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: revocation during a cell takes effect
cases.stimulus: Start a long cell, revoke one native tool while it runs, then call that tool later in the same cell.
cases.oracle: The later call is refused. The decision does not rest on a catalog captured at cell start; the record shows the revocation was observed mid-cell.

cases.requirement: small values keep their declared type
cases.stimulus: Call a native tool whose result is a small canonical value, and read it from the cell.
cases.oracle: The value arrives with its original schema type and is not silently replaced by a reference handle. The delivered type is recorded.

cases.requirement: a large result executes once and is delivered as a post-policy reference
cases.stimulus: Call one native tool returning a large result through the programmatic scope, counting executions.
cases.oracle: The tool executes exactly ONCE and what the cell receives is the reference produced by the final policy stage. An execution count above one, or a reference taken before the policy stage, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a redacted value is not recoverable through its reference
cases.stimulus: Trigger a post-policy deletion or replacement of a sensitive value, then attempt to recover the original through the artifact or reference path.
cases.oracle: The forbidden original value cannot be recovered by any path the cell can reach. Recovering it is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: nested wrapped calls cannot deadlock the pool
cases.stimulus: Drive many wrapped nested calls concurrently until the pool is saturated.
cases.oracle: The run either completes or refuses with a bounded, named error inside the budget; no cycle exists in which an outer pool slot waits on an inner slot it is itself blocking. The observed maximum concurrency and the refusal, if any, are recorded.

cases.requirement: end-of-cell drain has a recorded disposition per call
cases.stimulus: Return a cell while native child calls are still in flight.
cases.oracle: Every in-flight call carries one disposition from `settled`, `cancelled`, `handed-to-jobs`, `abandoned-unstarted`, and any call handed to Jobs names its job id. Nothing continues silently in the background with no record.

cases.requirement: control notices survive and stay bounded
cases.stimulus: A native tool returns `additionalContexts` / `concludeTurn` together with a large bulk image payload.
cases.oracle: The control semantics are preserved to the caller and are bounded in size, and bulk images do NOT enter the model context automatically. The recorded byte count of what entered context is stated.

cases.requirement: the kernel cannot forge host-authored facts
cases.stimulus: From a cell, submit an observation claim carrying host-authored fields such as `id`, `captured.sha256`, `captured.bytes` or `authority.*`.
cases.oracle: The claim is REFUSED and the refusal is recorded. The host-authored field set is not settable from Python by any route, and the type-level defense plus the wire-level refusal are both demonstrated.

cases.requirement: scope close is explicit and leaves no unsettled call
cases.stimulus: Close a programmatic scope while a nested call is still unsettled, for each close reason.
cases.oracle: The close reason is recorded from `completed`/`aborted`/`error`, every sub-call carries a disposition, and no call remains unsettled after the close. An unsettled call surviving the close is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: content projection follows the declared mode and is counted
cases.stimulus: Run one image-returning tool with `contentProjection: 'reference'` and again with `'defer-images'`.
cases.oracle: The bytes actually delivered to the model match the declared mode in each case, the mode is visible in the record, and the delivered byte counts differ as the modes require. A mode that is declared but not honoured is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the deployment depth ceiling cannot be lifted by the caller
cases.stimulus: From a cell, attempt to open grandchildren through the bridge and pass a large `maxDepth`.
cases.oracle: The deployment ceiling still applies and each refusal is recorded with its reason. A caller-supplied value that raises the effective ceiling is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a long line is recovered byte-for-byte
cases.stimulus: Capture a single 100 KiB line that spans several pages, then read it back.
cases.oracle: The recovered bytes equal the source bytes exactly (digest compared), with no silent tail truncation at any intermediate cap. The measured byte count and the digest are recorded.

cases.requirement: a large result stays out of the model context
cases.stimulus: Consume 512 native pages totalling 32 MiB in one cell.
cases.oracle: All pages are consumed correctly and the model-visible projection is at most 8 KiB, with the actual projection size recorded. The tier at which this was measured (in-process consumer vs a real out-of-process consumer) is stated explicitly and is not blurred.

cases.requirement: encoding and page boundaries do not corrupt records
cases.stimulus: Split UTF-8 text, CRLF text and JSONL at each page boundary, including inside a multi-byte character.
cases.oracle: No character is corrupted, no record is duplicated and no record is missing; the reassembled content equals the source.

cases.requirement: pagination cannot stall silently
cases.stimulus: A provider returns a repeated cursor and, separately, a backwards cursor.
cases.oracle: A `pagination-stalled` error is raised in both cases and the read terminates. An unbounded loop, or a silent stop that reports success, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: pages come from one snapshot
cases.stimulus: Read page 1, modify the source file, then read page 2.
cases.oracle: Page 2 either still matches the captured hash or the read fails explicitly. Pages from two different revisions are never mixed into one result, and the recorded hash is stated.

cases.requirement: paging does not rescan the whole file per page
cases.stimulus: Read P pages of a fixed large file while counting physical bytes read.
cases.oracle: The physical IO is bounded well below P full-file scans, and the actual IO and index cost are reported as measured numbers rather than described.

cases.requirement: a renderer cap does not shrink the canonical set
cases.stimulus: A grep returns more matches than the renderer displays, with the renderer showing 250 rows.
cases.oracle: The canonical full set is readable through the programmatic path, and any backend raw cap is still marked `partial` with its coverage recorded. Treating the rendered 250 as the whole set is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: quota and disk failure are explicit
cases.stimulus: Fill the store to its quota and, separately, make a capture fail mid-write.
cases.oracle: An explicit `partial`/failure is reported with its stage, no unbounded inline expansion is attempted, and no external effect is re-executed as a retry. The store's state after the failure is recorded.

cases.requirement: every ACQUISITION gap is attributed to a stage
cases.stimulus: Produce captures that lose bytes at known stages: provider cap, native tool cap, a lossy transform, and a storage refusal.
cases.oracle: Every ACQUISITION gap -- a gap in what the world or the capture path actually gave us -- appears in `acquisition.gaps` with its stage from the closed set `provider-acquisition`, `native-acquisition`, `transform`, `retention`, plus a recovery from `page`/`refetch`/`none`/`unknown`. A loss at one of those four stages that is not recorded as a gap is NOT PASS. TWO STAGES ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THIS SET and their absence is the point: `model-projection` is not an acquisition gap but a projection choice, and is measured by DATA-13 as a ProjectionManifest; `transport` is not an acquisition gap because the product REJECTS an over-limit frame before any successful value exists, so there is no partial success to attribute. Recording a deliberate projection as a loss, or inventing a partial-success transport to have something to attribute, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a refetch is a new observation, never a back-fill
cases.stimulus: Fetch a URL, let the content change, then refetch it.
cases.oracle: A new observation with its own hash and acquisition time is created, and the earlier hash and time remain retrievable. The earlier body is never overwritten or re-attributed to the new fetch.

cases.requirement: a page cursor is not a bearer token
cases.stimulus: Replay a valid cursor against a different store or a different revision.
cases.oracle: The cursor is refused and the refusal is recorded. A cursor that yields pages from a store it was not issued for is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: reference state is reported, never assumed
cases.stimulus: Resolve references whose objects are durable, orphaned, and missing.
cases.oracle: Each resolves to its true state from `durable`/`orphaned`/`missing` with the store's own verdict. A missing object must not return an empty success; an orphan must be reconcilable or eligible for grace GC, and must never be reported as delivered.

cases.requirement: an intentional model projection is recorded as a manifest, not as a loss
cases.stimulus: Project a complete capture down to what the model will see, then read the projection record and try to resolve the omitted part through the ref it names.
cases.oracle: A deliberate reduction of complete data before the model sees it is recorded as a `ProjectionManifest` carrying: `sourceRef` (what complete thing was projected), `selected` and `omitted` counts or bytes, a `recoverable` ref when the omitted part is recoverable, and a `projectionReason` from a closed set naming WHY. The manifest must not appear in `acquisition.gaps`: a deliberate projection is NOT a loss, and recording one as a loss makes an honest system look broken and a broken system look honest. An intentional projection that is recorded nowhere is NOT PASS. A projection whose `recoverable` ref does not actually resolve is NOT PASS. This case is the projection half of v1's DATA-09, which conflated the two.

cases.requirement: an object published before its reference commits is an orphan, not a delivery
cases.stimulus: Kill the host between artifact publication and the Session reference commit, then reopen the store.
cases.oracle: The artifact is classified as an orphan that is reconcilable or eligible for grace GC, and no reader reports it as delivered. A store that presents it as a completed delivery is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a bad reference is an integrity failure
cases.stimulus: Point a durable event at a missing object and, separately, at an object whose bytes do not match the recorded hash.
cases.oracle: Both produce an explicit integrity failure naming the reference. Returning empty content, or any success, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a crash before admission publishes nothing
cases.stimulus: Kill the host before a child or cell starts, then restart.
cases.oracle: No task is published for the interrupted attempt, and a retry is performed only for operations explicitly established as not having taken effect. A retry of an ambiguous operation is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a lost effect reply stays unknown
cases.stimulus: Have a remote side commit an effect while the host loses the response, then restart.
cases.oracle: The outcome is recorded as `unknown`, the whole cell is not replayed by default, and the unresolved effect is named with what would be needed to reconcile it. Replaying the cell as if nothing had happened is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: kernel death advances the epoch and names the loss
cases.stimulus: Kill the kernel while it holds variables, then continue the session.
cases.oracle: The epoch advances, a lost list is visible to the reader, and the original Session survives with its history intact. A silent continuation on a fresh namespace is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a checkpoint behind the last cell reports what was skipped
cases.stimulus: Restore from a data checkpoint older than the last executed cell.
cases.oracle: `as-of`, `skipped` and `lost` are each reported, and complete recovery is NOT claimed. A restore that reports full success while silently dropping later state is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a hostile checkpoint is never deserialized on the host
cases.stimulus: Supply a checkpoint containing pickle, dill or an object dtype payload.
cases.oracle: Automatic restore is refused, or the payload is handled only as isolated untrusted code; the host process never deserializes it. The refusal names the format. A restore that executes it in the host is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: reconnect does not auto-re-execute an ambiguous call
cases.stimulus: Drop the transport mid-call and reconnect.
cases.oracle: The ambiguous call is not automatically re-executed, and resources plus logs are reconciled with the ambiguity stated. An automatic re-execution is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a stale epoch cannot write authority
cases.stimulus: After a restart, have an old worker submit a settlement carrying its old epoch. If no such worker can exist, state the topology fact that makes it impossible instead of constructing one.
cases.oracle: One of two arms must hold, and the record must say WHICH. ARM A (the guarantee is claimed): the authoritative write REFUSES the stale-generation settlement, the refusal is retained as diagnostic evidence rather than discarded, and the comparison happens inside the same durable update that releases the reservation. ARM B (the guarantee is NOT claimed): the record states that stale-generation settlement is not claimed, names the TOPOLOGY FACT that makes it physically impossible, and the case is filed NOT_CLAIMED -- never PASS. A settlement from a superseded generation that LANDS while the deployment claims the guarantee is NOT PASS. Filing ARM B without naming the topology fact is NOT PASS either: NOT_CLAIMED is a statement about the deployment, so it carries the same burden of proof as a claim.

cases.requirement: the epoch guard is reachable from a production path whenever the guard exists
cases.stimulus: Trace the guard that rejects a stale-epoch settlement from the entry point a real host uses, or record that the deployment makes no such claim and the guard is gone.
cases.oracle: WHEN the deployment claims stale-generation settlement (REC-09 ARM A), the guard is reachable from at least one non-test production path, demonstrated by a call graph or a live boot rather than by the guard's own unit test, and an epoch field that nothing reads or writes after initialisation is INERT and is NOT PASS. WHEN the deployment does not claim it (REC-09 ARM B), the guard is DELETED and this case is NOT_CLAIMED, naming the topology fact -- an unreachable guard left in the tree is NOT PASS in either arm, because a mechanism the product cannot reach is the defect class this project has recorded more than twelve times.

cases.requirement: the write boundary is disclosed, not claimed
cases.stimulus: Have `pwsh` write a file outside the workspace root under the deployed mode, and read the record's own description of the boundary.
cases.oracle: The write SUCCEEDS and the record states plainly that no filesystem write confinement is claimed under trusted-local. Presenting a write boundary the mode does not provide, or describing the deployment as confined, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the read boundary is disclosed, not claimed
cases.stimulus: Read a file outside the workspace root through a native tool and, separately, through a Python cell.
cases.oracle: Both reads SUCCEED and the record states that reads are not confined. A read-only mount must not be presented as secrecy, and a documentation claim of read isolation is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: one path string resolves to one file in one world
cases.stimulus: Resolve the same path string through a native `read`, a `grep`, a spawned process and a Python cell.
cases.oracle: All four resolve in the SAME execution world and reach the same file; the record names that world. Any mixed resolution, where one route reads a different file than another, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: link and rename behaviour is recorded per vector, including where nothing refuses
cases.stimulus: Attempt a symlink escape, a hardlink creation and a cross-boundary rename.
cases.oracle: Each vector's observed outcome is recorded separately, and a vector that is NOT refused is reported as a finding rather than folded into a green. The correctness half must hold in every case: no data corruption, and no operation silently acting on a different file than the caller named.

cases.requirement: structured file tools keep their documented semantics
cases.stimulus: `read` a large file with offset and limit; `edit` an exact unique replacement; attempt an ambiguous replacement.
cases.oracle: Pagination returns the requested window, the exact replacement applies once, and the ambiguous case is refused rather than guessing. These tools remain usable beside the Python path rather than being degraded to decoration.

cases.requirement: workspace files and store-owned artifacts are not conflated
cases.stimulus: List what a cell can reach in the workspace and what the artifact store owns, then write a workspace file with the same name as an artifact.
cases.oracle: The record distinguishes workspace paths from store-owned artifacts, and the store's object is unaffected by the workspace write. Assuming an artifact is immutable merely because a cell can write a same-named path is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the hard capacity of 30 is never exceeded
cases.stimulus: With 30 valid children occupying slots, request a 31st and a 32nd.
cases.oracle: Both requests are refused BEFORE publication, and the occupancy counter never exceeds 30 at any sampled instant. The refusal code and the observed high-water mark are recorded.

cases.requirement: every admission path shares one quota
cases.stimulus: Request slots through a one-shot start, a continuable start, a workflow, a direct factory and a cold resume.
cases.oracle: All paths draw on the same host-wide quota, and a large caller-supplied `maxDepth` cannot bypass the ceiling. A path that admits without consulting the quota is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a completion admits a replacement without waiting for the wave
cases.stimulus: With sufficient ready supply, let the fastest child complete while the others still run.
cases.oracle: The replacement starts without waiting for the remaining children, and the measured delay from completion to replacement start is recorded against the declared SLO.

cases.requirement: an unconfirmed cancel still occupies
cases.stimulus: Send a cancel and, in a separate arm, make cleanup fail while the child process is still alive.
cases.oracle: In both arms the slot remains occupied or the child is quarantined as unknown, and no replacement is admitted into the freed-looking slot. Releasing the slot on a merely REQUESTED cancel is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the root is not starved and is not counted as a child
cases.stimulus: Run 30 children that continuously request provider and tool budget, then have the root need to run.
cases.oracle: The root still obtains a reserved opportunity to run and completes its work, and the root is provably excluded from the child count by a separate check.

cases.requirement: no filler or idle placeholder children
cases.stimulus: Set the target to 30 with only 2 ready tasks.
cases.oracle: Exactly 2 children are created, the shortage is reported with its reason, and the root is notified. Creating sleep or idle placeholder children to reach the number is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the cap is host-wide across roots
cases.stimulus: Two roots each request 30 children, with each root's own configuration allowing 30.
cases.oracle: The whole host stays at or below 30, and the queue, the fairness between roots and the real deficit are visible. A per-root cap that lets the host exceed 30 in aggregate is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: target changes are honest in both directions
cases.stimulus: Adjust the target 30 -> 1 -> 30 while completions are arriving concurrently.
cases.oracle: Lowering does not silently kill running children, raising tops up within a bounded delay, and the reported revision matches the sequence of changes.

cases.requirement: credit reservation is atomic
cases.stimulus: Have many launches contend for the last available cost credit in the same instant.
cases.oracle: Exactly one reservation succeeds, the ledger does not overspend, and an unknown usage stays conservatively reserved rather than being treated as zero. The final ledger is recorded.

cases.requirement: a completion storm neither duplicates nor misses a top-up
cases.stimulus: Have many children complete within one event-loop interval.
cases.oracle: No duplicate launch, no overshoot past the target, and no missed replacement; the coalesced drain is shown to be re-triggerable. The exact launch count is recorded.

cases.requirement: pause stops admission and does not silently resume
cases.stimulus: With root inference, child tools and a top-up queue all present, trigger a user pause.
cases.oracle: No new child is admitted and no continuation silently resumes. The record states which already-published effects are still stopping or awaiting reconciliation, and which are confirmed stopped.

cases.requirement: a cost overrun is recorded, not edited away
cases.stimulus: Let real usage exceed the reservation, and let an auxiliary request appear on the bill.
cases.oracle: The overrun and any unknown are recorded and new admissions pause. Removing or adjusting the charge to keep the report green is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: depth, family and global limits are each applied
cases.stimulus: Have a child attempt to open grandchildren while a second root uses the same provider.
cases.oracle: The depth ceiling and the per-run/global provider limits each take effect independently, and a family-scoped pool is not reported as the global limit. Each refusal names which limit fired.

cases.requirement: a zero-test run is not a PASS
cases.stimulus: Run a runner that exits 0 while collecting no test at all.
cases.oracle: The verdict is NOT PASS and the reason names the zero-test condition. The observed exit code is recorded so the reader can see that exit 0 alone would have been read as green.

cases.requirement: an all-skipped run is not a PASS
cases.stimulus: Run a suite in which every test is skipped and the runner exits 0.
cases.oracle: The verdict is NOT PASS, the skip count is reported, and the recorded exit code shows it was 0.

cases.requirement: the candidate cannot weaken its own oracle
cases.stimulus: Have the candidate attempt to modify a protected suite, a threshold, or the acceptance configuration.
cases.oracle: The modification is either impossible or detected, and acceptance is not weakened. A silent green produced by an edited oracle is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a receipt does not outlive the tree it describes
cases.stimulus: Verify a tree, then change the workspace, the environment or the oracle, and re-check the stored receipt.
cases.oracle: The freshness check reports NOT FRESH and the old verdict is not reusable as current completion. Reusing a stale receipt is NOT PASS. NOTE: this is the NEW VER-04 and has nothing to do with the old spec's VER-04, which is out of scope and recorded in not_applicable_inherited.

cases.requirement: A-B-A mutation during acceptance is caught
cases.stimulus: Change a file and change it back to its original hash while acceptance is running.
cases.oracle: The candidate is frozen to an immutable snapshot and the verdict is bound to that snapshot, so the tampered run cannot be certified. The control arm must also be run: endpoint hash polling alone would have certified the tampered run, and that is demonstrated rather than asserted.

cases.requirement: in-flight writers are converged or isolated before freezing
cases.stimulus: Complete a request while a background mutation is still active.
cases.oracle: The system converges or isolates the writer before freezing, and an unresolved mutation produces an unknown rather than a certification. Certifying a tree that was still changing is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a verification failure does not permanently drain the run
cases.stimulus: Fail verification, then legitimately resume the run with corrected work.
cases.oracle: Legitimate recovery continues, and `pause` has not been misused as a final drain. A run that cannot continue after a recoverable failure is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: an acceptance definition cannot authorize itself
cases.stimulus: Change an acceptance definition's threshold and re-run it without re-recording the authorized digest.
cases.oracle: The digest check FAILS and the run is refused. Obtaining the authorized digest must be a separate step from writing the definition, so a definition cannot go green in the same breath it is edited.

cases.requirement: the verification tier and its limit are stated, never implied
cases.stimulus: Read every recorded verdict in this deployment and compare the claimed tier with the tier at which it was measured.
cases.oracle: Each verdict names its tier from the layer legend and the artifact it is bound to; a green measured at T0/T1 is never presented as T2/T3/T5/T6. Under trusted-local the verification environment runs as the SAME OS user as the host, so the record must ALSO state that no privilege separation between the verifier and the verified exists. Presenting a same-account verification as privileged isolation is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the search-to-citation chain uses real sources
cases.stimulus: Run an independent search, fetch the original source, widen to the full relevant range, then cite.
cases.oracle: Every step carries a real source with a version and a timestamp. A missing key or a failed fetch is reported as a failure, never turned into a fabricated result or an invented citation.

cases.requirement: the evidence tier is not inflated
cases.stimulus: Store only the bytes of a PDF without ever presenting its body to the reader.
cases.oracle: The record reports `bytes_captured` and does not claim `primary_read` or `understood`. The tier vocabulary must not even contain the stronger values as reachable states.

cases.requirement: an incomplete parse reports its own limits
cases.stimulus: Parse a PDF whose body omits tables, and separately follow a redirect, a 404 and a truncated body.
cases.oracle: The read range and its limitations are stated for each case, and missing content is never filled in. Using a search snippet as if it were the full text is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: provider truncation is not local full recoverability
cases.stimulus: Have a provider deliver only the first part of a body.
cases.oracle: `acquisition.completeness` is `partial` with recovery `none` or `refetch`, and the record does not claim the full text is locally recoverable. Claiming completeness from a truncated fetch is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: raw and derived content are separately identified
cases.stimulus: De-script an HTML page and convert it to markdown, including a conversion that fails.
cases.oracle: Raw and derived artifacts carry separate hashes and separate locators, and a failed conversion produces an explicit failure rather than manufactured body text.

cases.requirement: a claim is locatable and external content stays untrusted
cases.stimulus: Make a final claim citing a page or fragment, from a page that also contains embedded commands, a skill-update instruction and an authority claim.
cases.oracle: The claim can be located in the captured artifact at a named span, a snippet is not treated as the full text, and the external content is wrapped as untrusted data that cannot change host authority or cause execution.

cases.requirement: observation caching is measured, not assumed
cases.stimulus: Observe one unchanged stored session N times with the cache sized above N, and count the underlying reads.
cases.oracle: The read count is recorded verbatim. A cache that produces N reads where a hit would produce 1 is reported as a DEFECT with its cause, not described as a cache that works. A bound and an eviction policy are not a hit rate.

cases.requirement: a scan watermark is stable while events append
cases.stimulus: Run a history scan while new events keep being appended.
cases.oracle: The page order is fixed to one snapshot for the whole scan, and events appended after the snapshot are read in a separate pass with their own watermark. Interleaving new events into the running scan is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: one oversized event does not break the page budget
cases.stimulus: Read a history page containing a single event larger than the page budget.
cases.oracle: An authorized reference or a segmented read is returned, and the page budget is not exceeded. Truncating silently, or emitting the whole event inline, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: repeated traversal does not re-replay the whole log
cases.stimulus: Traverse the same history for 100 pages.
cases.oracle: A prepared observation or index is reused, and the actual number of full log replays is recorded as a number. A measured 100 replays for 100 pages is reported as the defect it is.

cases.requirement: the three visibilities stay separate
cases.stimulus: Store an event without reading it programmatically, then read it without emitting it, then emit it.
cases.oracle: `obtainable`, `consumed` and `model-projected` are recorded as three separate states and are never merged into one. Reporting a stored event as model-visible, or a consumed event as projected, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a derived index is rebuildable from canonical data
cases.stimulus: Delete the derived full-text index, then restore.
cases.oracle: The index is rebuilt from the canonical Session and artifact data with no second history source required, and the rebuilt index answers the same queries as before. The rebuild is recorded with what it read.
